about: Superhuman, formerly Grammarly, is a US AI-powered productivity company headquartered in San Francisco, which merged its Grammarly writing assistant with the Superhuman email client and Coda in 2025 under the Superhuman name. Grammarly's tools reach tens of millions of daily users, and it has raised large funding rounds including a 1 billion dollar financing from General Catalyst in 2025. Customers are individuals and businesses buying subscriptions. Very strong consumer awareness through heavy digital advertising.

Chainguard is a US software supply chain security company based in Kirkland, Washington that sells minimal, hardened container images, libraries and tools, built on its own Wolfi Linux distribution, to enterprises and developers. Founded 2021 by former Google engineers, it has raised funding at a valuation of several billion dollars from venture investors. Revenue comes from subscriptions. B2B developer brand known in cloud security communities but not to consumers.

wiki.title: Gear case
wiki.text: A gear case, also known as a chain case or chain guard, is a protective enclosure for the bicycle's chain and sprocket assemblies. Its primary function is to protect the cyclist from being soiled or trapped in the chain rings while also protecting the chain from dirt and moisture. Gear cases may fully or partially enclose the drivetrain and sometimes incorporate an oil bath for continuous lubrication. Modern examples are usually moulded in plastic. Although they are also used by some touring bicycles as well as some chain-drive machinery, chain cases are most frequently found on utility bicycles.

about: Cohesity is a US data security and management company headquartered in San Jose/Santa Clara, California, selling backup, recovery, ransomware protection and AI-based data insight on its platform. It combined with Veritas's enterprise data protection business in 2024. Customers are enterprises and governments globally. Founded 2013 by Mohit Aron, with investors including SoftBank and Sequoia. Revenue is in the order of 1.5 billion dollars. B2B technology brand known to IT professionals.

wiki.title: Cohesity
wiki.what: American developer of data management software
wiki.text: Cohesity, Inc. is an American privately held information technology company headquartered in Santa Clara, California, with offices in India and Ireland. The company develops software that allows IT professionals to backup, manage and gain insights from their data across multiple systems or cloud providers. Their products also include anti-ransomware features, Disaster Recovery-as-a-Service, and SaaS management.

about: Commvault is a US data protection and cyber resilience software company headquartered in Tinton Falls, New Jersey and listed on Nasdaq (CVLT). It sells backup, recovery, cloud data management and ransomware recovery to enterprises and governments, delivered as software and SaaS (Metallic), with revenue near 1 billion dollars. Founded in 1996 as a spin-off from Bell Labs. Customers are IT departments in over 100 countries. B2B brand, known to IT professionals.

wiki.title: Commvault
wiki.text: Commvault Systems, Inc. is an American publicly traded cybersecurity and data protection software company. Commvault's services are used for data security, as well as cloud and infrastructure management.

about: Cybereason is a cybersecurity company offering endpoint detection and response, extended detection and response and managed threat hunting through its AI-driven platform. Headquartered in Boston with an Israeli research base in Tel Aviv, it was founded in 2012 and is backed by SoftBank and Liberty Strategic Capital; it merged with Trustwave in 2025. Customers are enterprises and managed service providers. B2B security brand with limited consumer awareness.

wiki.title: Cybereason
wiki.text: Cybereason is an American cybersecurity technology company founded in 2012. It has offices in La Jolla, California ; London, UK ; Tel Aviv, Israel; and several others around the world.

about: Luma AI is a US generative AI company based in Palo Alto, California that develops 3D capture and video-generation models, including Dream Machine and Ray video models, for creatives, studios and enterprises. Founded 2021, it raised a 900 million dollar round in 2025 led by Humain (Saudi Arabia) with AMD participation, valuing it near 4 billion dollars. Revenue comes from subscriptions and enterprise licences. Well known in creative technology and AI circles.

wiki.title: Dream Machine (text-to-video model)
wiki.text: Dream Machine was a text-to-video model created by Luma Labs and launched in June 2024. It generates video output based on user prompts or still images. Dream Machine has been noted for its ability to realistically capture motion, while some critics have remarked upon the lack of transparency about its training data.

about: Uniphore is a US enterprise AI company headquartered in Palo Alto, California, with major development in Chennai, India, founded in 2008. It sells conversational AI, speech analytics and agentic automation for contact centres and customer service teams, through the Business AI Cloud platform, and acquired Emotion Research Lab, Jacada and Orby. It raised funds at a roughly 2.5 billion dollar valuation, backed by Nvidia, Snowflake and AMD. B2B brand with little consumer awareness.

wiki.title: Uniphore
wiki.text: Uniphore is an American software company that develops artificial intelligence platforms for business use. The company is headquartered in Palo Alto, California, with offices in the United States, United Kingdom, Spain, Israel, United Arab Emirates, and India. Uniphore is known for its "Business AI Cloud," an enterprise AI platform that combines data, knowledge, models, and software agents for use in sales, marketing, and service. The company has also acquired firms in video emotion AI, AI agents, low-code automation, knowledge automation, voice and screen capture, customer data platforms, and data engineering.

about: Wispr Flow is a San Francisco-based software startup that provides AI-powered voice dictation across apps and devices, turning speech into polished text in any text field on Mac, Windows and iOS. Founded around 2021, it has raised venture funding from investors such as Menlo Ventures. Customers are professionals and teams subscribing for a monthly fee. Growing tech-consumer brand with limited mass awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)
cb_desc: Wispr Flow provides Al- powered voice dictation and...

wiki.title: Wispr Flow
wiki.text: Wispr Flow is a speech recognition and dictation software application developed by Wispr AI. It converts spoken language into text across multiple platforms, including macOS, Windows, iOS, and Android. The software integrates with system-level input fields, allowing voice input in various applications.

about: Lovable is a Swedish AI software startup based in Stockholm, founded in 2023, whose platform lets users build web apps and websites by describing them in natural language, aimed at non-programmers and developers. It grew to tens of millions of dollars of annual revenue very quickly and raised funding at a valuation of several billion dollars from investors such as Accel and Creandum. Customers are individuals, startups and companies paying subscriptions. High-profile tech brand in the AI start-up scene.

wiki.title: Lovable (company)
wiki.what: Swedish vibe coding platform and company
wiki.text: Lovable is a Swedish vibe coding platform and company. Founded in Stockholm in 2023, it provides software that allows users to enter prompts to automate software development.

about: Aura is a US consumer digital safety company based in Boston that offers identity theft protection, credit monitoring, VPN, antivirus and parental controls bundled in a subscription, serving millions of subscribers. Formed in 2021 when Intersections combined with Aura, backed by Warburg Pincus. Revenue comes from subscriptions. Strong consumer brand through heavy digital advertising.

EliseAI is a US software company based in New York that sells conversational AI for property management and healthcare, automating leasing, tenant communications, maintenance requests and appointment scheduling for large apartment owners and health providers. Founded 2017, it raised funding at a valuation of over 2 billion dollars led by Andreessen Horowitz. Revenue comes from software subscriptions. B2B brand known to the real estate and property technology industry, not consumers.

Enveda is a US biotech company based in Boulder, Colorado, which uses machine learning and analytical chemistry to discover medicines from natural compounds found in plants, with a pipeline of small molecules for inflammatory and metabolic conditions. Founded 2019, it has raised hundreds of millions of dollars from investors including Premji Invest, Lux and Kinnevik at a valuation over 1 billion dollars. Customers would be pharmaceutical partners. Pre-revenue biotech with no consumer brand awareness.
cb_desc: Enveda discovers medicines by studying the chemistry of...

about: Oratomic is a Pasadena, California company that, according to its Crunchbase listing, develops neutral-atom quantum hardware and error-correction technology. Funding, team, products and customers are not confirmed from the input. Pre-commercial deep-tech with no known public awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)
cb_desc: Oratomic develops neutral-atom quantum hardware and error-..

about: Oxide Computer Company is a US hardware and software startup based in Emeryville, California that builds rack-scale servers for on-premises cloud computing, with its own firmware, hypervisor and control plane. Founded 2019 by former Joyent and Sun engineers Steve Tuck and Bryan Cantrill, it has raised funds from Eclipse, Intel Capital and USV. Customers are enterprises and government. B2B infrastructure vendor with a cult following among engineers, not consumers.

Replit is a US cloud-based software development platform headquartered in Foster City, California, offering a browser IDE and the Replit Agent AI tool that builds apps from plain language prompts. It serves tens of millions of developers, students and non-coders, reaching annual recurring revenue in the hundreds of millions of dollars in 2025 and a valuation of about 3 billion dollars after backing from a16z, Y Combinator and Craft Ventures. Founded 2016. Strong developer and AI consumer brand.

wiki.title: Replit
wiki.text: Replit, formerly Repl.it, is an American technology company that operates a cloud-based platform for writing and running software. Founded in 2016, the company first developed a browser-based Online integrated development environment (IDE) that supported multiple programming languages. It later added tools that use artificial intelligence to generate code.

about: Sigma Computing is a US cloud analytics and business intelligence company headquartered in San Francisco that lets business users explore and analyse data in cloud warehouses such as Snowflake and Databricks through a spreadsheet-like interface, with AI features. Customers include thousands of enterprises. Founded 2014, it has raised funds from Sutter Hill, Snowflake Ventures and Spark Capital, at a valuation reported above 1 billion dollars. Revenue is subscription software. B2B brand known in data teams.

wiki.title: Sigma (analytics company)
wiki.what: American analytics and business intelligence company
wiki.text: Sigma is an American cloud-based analytics and business intelligence company. Sigma was founded in 2014 by Jason Frantz and Rob Woollen.

about: Skydio is a US drone maker based in San Mateo, California, which builds autonomous AI-powered drones such as the X10, used by US and allied police, fire, military and infrastructure inspection customers, and is one of the largest American drone makers. Founded 2014 by former MIT researchers, it has raised funds from Andreessen Horowitz, Nvidia and Next47 at a valuation of about 2.2 billion dollars. Chinese sanctions on its battery supplier hit it in 2024. B2B and government brand with growing profile.

wiki.title: Skydio
wiki.what: American UAV manufacturer based in San Mateo
wiki.text: Skydio, Inc. is an American manufacturer of drones headquartered in San Mateo, California. The company manufactures drones for use in battlefield situation awareness, policing, and inspection. Their drones can complete fully autonomous missions with the use of a dock to automatically recharge.

about: Spire Global is a US space-to-cloud data analytics company headquartered in Vienna, Virginia and listed on the NYSE (SPIR), operating a fleet of small satellites that collect maritime, aviation and weather data and sells it to shipping companies, governments, insurers and logistics firms. It has about 100 satellites and revenue near 100 million dollars. Founded 2012 as NanoSatisfi. B2B data brand known in space and analytics circles, not by the public.

wiki.title: Spire Global
wiki.text: Spire Global, Inc. is a space-to-cloud data and analytics company that specializes in the tracking of global data sets powered by a large constellation of nanosatellites, such as the tracking of maritime, aviation and weather patterns.

about: Upstage is an AI company building large language models and document-processing AI. Its products include the Solar family of language models and Document Parse, used by enterprises to extract data from documents. Customers are mainly businesses in finance, insurance and public sector, selling through API access and enterprise licences. Founded in 2020 and run from South Korea, with a San Jose, California listing in Crunchbase. It has raised about $735 million in total funding, the latest round in October 2026. Private and B2B, with little consumer brand awareness.

wiki.title: Upstage (company)
wiki.text: Upstage Co., Ltd. is a South Korean artificial intelligence company founded in 2020.

about: Upwind Security provides a cloud-native application protection platform, unifying cloud and application security so enterprises can detect threats and risks at runtime across their cloud workloads. Customers are mid-size and large businesses that run on public cloud, paying through software subscriptions. Founded in 2022 by Israeli founders, with its US base in San Francisco. It has raised about $830 million in total funding, the latest round in September 2026. Private, B2B, with little public brand awareness outside the cybersecurity community.
cb_desc: Upwind Security provides unified cloud and application...

about: Wonderful develops an enterprise AI platform, according to Crunchbase, and is classified under agentic AI and AI infrastructure. It is listed with an Amsterdam, Netherlands headquarters. It has raised about $848 million in total funding, with its most recent round in September 2026, so it is a heavily funded private company. Specific products, customers and revenue model are not given in the available data. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

about: Coralogix is a SaaS observability and security platform that uses machine learning to analyse logs, metrics and traces without requiring customers to pay to index all data first. Customers are software and technology companies, who pay for subscriptions based on data volume. Founded in 2014 in Israel, with a Boston headquarters. Has raised about $551 million in total funding, with a valuation above $1 billion. Private. B2B brand, known to developers, with limited consumer visibility.

Fundbox is a US fintech that provides small business financing, including lines of credit, net-terms and invoice financing, delivered via integrations with accounting and commerce platforms and underwritten by its own data models. Customers are small and mid-size US businesses, and revenue comes from fees and interest. Founded in 2013 and based in San Francisco. Has raised about $553 million in total funding, much of it debt. Private. B2B brand with limited consumer awareness.

wiki.title: Fundbox
wiki.text: Fundbox is a working capital platform based in San Francisco that offers credit and payments as a service to small businesses. Founded in 2013, the company innovates technology to help optimize cash flow for small businesses.

about: General Intuition is a frontier AI research lab based in New York that builds foundation models for spatial and temporal reasoning, trained on video game footage. It was spun out of Medal, the game-clip platform, in 2025, with Khosla Ventures backing. The aim is agents that can act in the physical and virtual worlds, with licensing and partnerships as likely revenue. Crunchbase shows about $674 million in total funding, latest September 2026. Private. B2B research brand, little public awareness.
cb_desc: General Intuition is a frontier research lab focused on...

about: Hyperscale Data, formerly Ault Alliance, is a diversified holding company that owns businesses in data centre and bitcoin mining operations, energy, lending and defence electronics, and holds investments in other companies. Based in Las Vegas, Nevada, and chaired by Milton Ault. Revenue is mixed across subsidiaries. Listed on NYSE American (GPUS). Crunchbase shows about $606 million in funding. Small-cap, with low consumer brand visibility.

Lila Sciences is a Cambridge, Massachusetts company building scientific superintelligence, combining AI models with autonomous labs ("AI science factories") to run experiments in life sciences, chemistry and materials. It emerged from Flagship Pioneering in 2025. Customers would be pharma and industrial partners via research collaborations and licensing. Crunchbase shows about $551 million in total funding, the latest in January 2026. Private. Scientific B2B brand with little public awareness.
cb_desc: Lila Sciences creates a scientific superintelligence...

about: Manus AI develops general-purpose AI agents that autonomously complete multi-step tasks such as research, coding and report creation. Launched in 2025 by Butterfly Effect, a startup with Chinese founders that relocated to Singapore. Meta announced an acquisition of Manus in December 2025. Revenue comes from subscriptions for individuals and professionals. Crunchbase shows about $585 million in total funding, latest October 2026. Well-known in the AI community, limited mainstream consumer awareness.

wiki.title: Manus (AI agent)
wiki.text: Manus is an autonomous artificial intelligence agent developed by Butterfly Effect, a company founded in China and based in Singapore.

about: ModelBest, known in Chinese as Mianbi Intelligence, is a Beijing-based AI company developing efficient large language models, notably the MiniCPM series of on-device models, spun out of Tsinghua University's NLP lab in 2022. It sells model acceleration and deployment to enterprises and device makers. Crunchbase shows about CN¥4.01 billion in total funding, the latest in July 2026. Private. B2B brand, known mostly in the Chinese AI community.

wiki.title: ModelBest
wiki.text: ModelBest Inc. is a Chinese artificial intelligence company based in the Haidian District of Beijing. The company originated from Tsinghua University's Natural Language Processing Laboratory and develops large language models and multimodal AI systems. Its products include the open-source MiniCPM series of AI models.

about: Mujin provides automation solutions for industrial robots, with its MujinOS controller and vision-based software allowing robots to pick, palletize and depalletize in warehouses and factories without manual teaching. Customers are logistics operators, e-commerce firms and manufacturers, with revenue from software, robot cells and services. Founded in 2011 and based in Tokyo, with offices in the US and Europe. Crunchbase shows about $635 million in total funding. Private. B2B industrial brand, little consumer awareness.

wiki.title: Muyijin
wiki.text: Muyijin is a village in Alvandkuh-e Gharbi Rural District of the Central District in Hamadan County, Hamadan province, Iran.

about: OLIX designs optical AI accelerators that use light-based computing to run AI workloads, according to Crunchbase. It is based in London, England, and is classified under Artificial Intelligence. It has raised about $562 million in total funding, with its latest round in August 2026, which is very large for a hardware startup of its type. Customers and revenue model are not stated. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

about: OneStream Software provides a unified cloud platform for corporate finance, covering consolidation, planning, reporting, analytics and AI-supported close processes. Customers are large enterprises and finance teams, paying subscriptions. Founded in 2010 and based in Birmingham, Michigan, with global customers. KKR invested heavily in 2021. It listed on Nasdaq (OS) in July 2024. Crunchbase shows about $665 million in funding. B2B software brand with limited consumer awareness.

PaleBlueDot AI is a technology company that provides cloud and AI compute services, according to Crunchbase. It is listed in Palo Alto, California, and classified under Artificial Intelligence. It has raised about $615 million in total funding, the latest round in October 2026. Customers, products and ownership are not detailed in the available data. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

about: Recursive is a San Francisco developer of self-improving AI systems, according to Crunchbase, classified under Artificial Intelligence. It has raised about $650 million in total funding, with its latest round in April 2026, so it is a heavily funded private AI lab. wiki.title: Recursion
wiki.what: Process of repeating items in a self-similar way
wiki.text: Recursion occurs when the definition of a concept or process depends on a simpler or previous version of itself. Recursion is used in a variety of disciplines ranging from linguistics to logic. The most common application of recursion is in mathematics and computer science, where a function being defined is applied within its own definition. While this apparently defines an infinite number of instances, it is often done in such a way that no infinite loop or infinite chain of references can occur.

about: Rezolve is a London-based provider of AI-driven commerce technology, including Brain Commerce, which gives retailers AI search and product discovery, plus mobile commerce, payments and image recognition (Rezolve Brain and Rezolve Lens). Customers are retailers and brands, with revenue from software and services. Listed on Nasdaq as RZLV since 2024 after a SPAC merger with Armada Acquisition Corp I. Crunchbase shows about $665 million in funding. B2B brand with little consumer awareness.

Rokid develops augmented reality glasses and smart-voice devices, including the Rokid Max and Rokid Glasses AI products, used for entertainment, learning and workplace tasks. Founded in 2014 in Hangzhou, China, and listed in Crunchbase with a Mountain View, California address. Customers are consumers and enterprises, with sales through online and retail channels, including crowdfunding launches. Crunchbase shows about $661 million in total funding. Private. Emerging consumer tech brand with international retail presence.

Fortune Brands Innovations, formerly Fortune Brands Home & Security, makes home products including Moen faucets, Master Lock padlocks, Therma-Tru doors, Larson storm doors, Fiberon decking and Fortune Brands security items. Customers are homeowners, builders and retailers such as Home Depot and Lowe's, with revenue of about $4.5 billion. Headquartered in Deerfield, Illinois, spun out of Beam in 2011. Listed on NYSE (FBIN). Moen and Master Lock are well-known consumer brands.

Nextdoor is a neighbourhood social network where verified residents share local recommendations, alerts, classifieds and events, with tens of millions of users in 11 countries. Revenue comes mainly from advertising from local and national brands, plus sponsored posts and local deals. Founded in 2008 and headquartered in San Francisco. Listed on NYSE (KIND) via a 2021 SPAC merger with Khosla Ventures Acquisition Co. II. Recognised consumer app in the US. Crunchbase shows about $724 million in funding.

wiki.title: Nextdoor
wiki.what: Hyperlocal social networking service for neighborhoods
wiki.text: Nextdoor Holdings, Inc. is an American company that operates a hyperlocal social networking service for neighborhoods. The company was founded in 2008 and is based in San Francisco, California. Nextdoor launched in the United States in October 2011. It is available in eleven countries as of May 2023. In 2024, the company claimed to have 88 million "neighbors" as members. By June 30, 2026, the company reported 110 million "neighbors" as members.

about: AppDirect is a cloud commerce and subscription management platform that lets telecoms, technology vendors and other companies sell and manage software, apps and cloud services via marketplaces. Customers are carriers like Deutsche Telekom and software vendors, with revenue from platform fees and transactions. Founded in 2009 and based in San Francisco. Has raised about $575 million in total funding. Private. B2B brand, low consumer awareness.

about: Notion is an all-in-one workspace app combining notes, documents, wikis, project management, databases and AI assistants, used by individuals, teams and large companies. Revenue comes from per-user subscriptions, with over 100 million users and a reported valuation of around $10 billion. Founded in 2013, with headquarters in San Francisco. Crunchbase shows about $343 million in total funding. Private. Very recognisable among knowledge workers and students, with heavy creator marketing.

New York-based software company, founded in Bucharest in 2005, selling robotic process automation and agentic automation to large enterprises and governments by subscription, with revenue around $1.5 billion. Listed on the NYSE (PATH). B2B brand with moderate awareness, and some sports marketing. Revenue is about $1.5 billion a year. UiPath has about 4,000 employees and thousands of customers, including banks, insurers and government agencies.

wiki.title: UiPath
wiki.text: UiPath Inc. is a Romanian-American multinational software company that develops artificial intelligence (AI) and agentic automation and orchestration software. The company's software enables the building and orchestration of AI agents to automate complex processes and workflows.

about: Canadian software and cybersecurity company from Waterloo, Ontario, once the maker of BlackBerry smartphones and now selling QNX embedded operating systems for cars and cybersecurity products. Customers are carmakers and enterprises; revenue about $500-600 million. Listed on the NYSE and TSX (BB). Historic consumer brand, but today a B2B supplier. The company also sells Cylance AI security, and the QNX operating system runs in tens of millions of vehicles.

wiki.title: Blackberry
wiki.text: A blackberry is an edible fruit produced by many species in the genus Rubus in the family Rosaceae, hybrids among these species within the subgenus Rubus, and hybrids between the subgenera Rubus and Idaeobatus. The taxonomy of blackberries has historically been confused because of hybridization and apomixis so that species have often been grouped together and called species aggregates.

wiki.title: BlackBerry Limited
wiki.text: BlackBerry Limited, formerly Research In Motion (RIM), is a Canadian software company specializing in secure communications and the Internet of Things (IoT). Founded in 1984, it was known for developing the BlackBerry brand of wireless mobile devices from 1999 to 2016. After the mobile division was spun off into BlackBerry Mobile in 2016 until its discontinuation in 2020, BlackBerry Limited transitioned to providing software and services and holds critical software application patents.

about: Edged US is a data centre company, listed in the input as based in Atlanta, which builds and operates sustainable, energy-efficient data centres for cloud and AI customers; it is a subsidiary of the Spanish telecom Telefonica group. Funding shown is $1.3 billion. B2B infrastructure brand with limited visibility. The input places it in the AI industry tag and in data centres, and no other details are given.

about: Legora is a Stockholm-based legal AI software company founded in 2023, selling an AI platform for lawyers to review, draft and research documents. Customers are law firms and legal departments, paying subscriptions. Valued at several billion dollars after 2025-26 funding. B2B brand with limited consumer awareness. The company has grown rapidly since its founding and works with major law firms in Europe and the US.
cb_desc: Legora develops an Al software platform to support legal....

wiki.title: Legora
wiki.text: Legora is a Swedish legal technology company. Founded in Stockholm in 2023 under the name Leya, it makes an artificial intelligence platform used by law firms for contract review, legal research and document drafting.

about: Digital experience platform company from New York and Stockholm, formed from Episerver and Optimizely, selling content management, experimentation and commerce software to enterprises. Owned by Insight Partners. Customers are marketers and retailers. B2B brand with moderate awareness in marketing technology. Revenue is subscription licences; the combined business serves thousands of customers worldwide. Optimizely has around 1,500 employees and offices in Europe, North America and Australia.

wiki.title: Optimizely
wiki.text: Optimizely is an AI platform purpose-built for enterprise marketing teams. They offer an agent platform to build and deploy AI agents, a content management system, agentic experimentation, A/B testing and multivariate testing tools, personalization, and feature toggle capabilities, as well as a content marketing platform and digital commerce solutions.

about: Software testing company with headquarters in Austin, Texas, and founded in Vienna in 2007, selling Tosca, qTest and Testim to enterprises for automated and AI-driven quality assurance. Backed by Insight Partners and SoftBank, with customers including large banks and carmakers. B2B brand with moderate awareness in IT. Tricentis has around 2,000 employees and thousands of customers worldwide, including large banks and insurers.

wiki.title: Tricentis
wiki.text: Tricentis is a software testing company founded in 2007 and headquartered in Austin, Texas. It provides software testing automation and software quality assurance products for enterprise software.

about: Dubai-headquartered, Istanbul-founded marketing technology company, founded 2012, selling the Insider One platform for personalised customer journeys, CDP and AI to retailers, banks and telecoms in dozens of countries. Became a unicorn after 2022 funding led by Sequoia India and General Atlantic. B2B brand, with limited consumer awareness. The input lists AI and marketing among its industries, and it has offices in Europe, the Middle East and Asia.

wiki.title: Insider One
wiki.text: Insider One is a software as a service (SaaS) company that develops software for customer engagement and marketing automation.

about: Santa Barbara-based hybrid observability platform, founded 2007, monitoring networks, servers, cloud and applications for enterprises and managed service providers. Customers are IT teams paying subscriptions. Backed by Vista Equity Partners and others, with a valuation around $2 billion. B2B brand with low consumer awareness. Operates globally with offices in the US, UK and Asia. LogicMonitor has thousands of customers and employs about 1,000 people worldwide.

Fremont, California-based IT distributor formed in 2021 by merging Tech Data and Synnex, supplying hardware, software, cloud and services to resellers and managed service providers in over 100 countries. Revenue is about $58 billion. Listed on the NYSE (SNX). B2B channel brand with low consumer awareness. TD SYNNEX has about 28,000 employees and works with technology vendors such as HP, Microsoft and Cisco.

wiki.title: TD Synnex
wiki.text: TD Synnex Corporation is an American IT distribution for 1,500 technology vendors. Headquartered in Fremont, California, the company has a workforce of 24,000 and 150,000 customers in over 100 countries. It was formed in 2021 by the merger of Synnex and Tech Data. TD SYNNEX is led by CEO Patrick Zammit.

about: Durham, North Carolina-based tax compliance software company, founded in 2004 in Washington state, automating sales tax, VAT and e-invoicing for businesses. Taken private in 2022 by Vista Equity Partners for about $8.4 billion after being listed on the NYSE. B2B brand with low consumer awareness. Avalara has about 5,000 employees, thousands of integrations and tens of thousands of customers in over 50 countries.

Jersey City-based data management and governance software company, founded 2001, selling AvePoint Confidence Platform to protect and manage Microsoft 365 and SaaS data for enterprises and governments. Listed on Nasdaq (AVPT). B2B brand with modest awareness outside IT. Customers are enterprises and public bodies adopting Microsoft 365 and AI tools, paying subscriptions. Operates offices across North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific.

wiki.title: AvePoint
wiki.text: AvePoint is a public company headquartered in Jersey City, New Jersey, United States. It develops software products intended to add features or security to other major platforms, like Microsoft 365, Google, or Salesforce. AvePoint was founded in 2001 and went public on NASDAQ in 2020.

about: Autonomous driving and delivery robots developer based in Austin, Texas, which spun out from Yandex's self-driving unit. Partners include Uber and Grubhub, and it has Nebius as a backer. Customers are ride-hailing and delivery platforms. Funding of about $850 million is shown. B2B with growing public awareness through robot deliveries. It runs sensors and vehicles in Texas and Europe, with Uber and Grubhub partners, and was backed by Nebius and Uber.

wiki.title: Avride
wiki.text: Avride Inc. is a developer of vehicular automation technology, including self-driving cars, robotaxis, and delivery robots. The company is headquartered in Austin, Texas and has additional offices in Tel Aviv, Israel; Belgrade, Serbia and Seoul, South Korea. It is a subsidiary of Nebius Group. Uber and Uber Eats use its self-driving cars and delivery robots in a few cities.

about: San Francisco-based background check software company, founded 2014, providing screening for employers and gig platforms such as Uber and Instacart, with API-first products. Valued about $5 billion. B2B brand with moderate public awareness. Customers are employers, staffing firms and gig-economy platforms that pay per check. Employs several hundred staff. Little consumer awareness beyond applicants who are screened. Checkr claims to process millions of background checks and works with thousands of customers including Uber, Lyft and Instacart.

Brooklyn-based blockchain software company founded 2014 by Ethereum co-founder Joseph Lubin, building MetaMask wallet, Linea network and Infura infrastructure. Customers are developers, enterprises and retail crypto users. The input shows Fort Worth. Strong brand in crypto circles and growing public name recognition. It earns revenue from infrastructure services, wallet swaps and enterprise consulting. ConsenSys employs a few hundred people and has run training courses and consulting for banks and governments.

wiki.title: Consensys
wiki.text: Consensys is a private blockchain software technology company founded by Joseph Lubin and based in Fort Worth.

about: San Francisco-based data company, founded 2018, selling Cribl Stream, Edge and Search for routing and managing telemetry and security data to enterprises. Valued about $3.5 billion. B2B brand, with modest awareness in IT and security. Customers are IT and security teams at large enterprises, who pay subscriptions. Mostly developer and security professional awareness, no public consumer profile. Cribl has about 1,000 employees, and its tools are used by security operations and observability teams.

Washington, DC-based information company using AI and data to provide policy, legal and regulatory analysis for government relations teams, listed on the NYSE (NOTE). Customers are corporates, governments and associations. B2B brand with limited public awareness. Customers are corporate affairs teams, law firms and governments, paying subscriptions. Little consumer awareness; listed on the NYSE. FiscalNote has about 600 employees and sells policy data and news services, including the CQ Roll Call brand.

wiki.title: FiscalNote
wiki.what: American software, data and media company
wiki.text: FiscalNote Holdings, Inc., or commonly FiscalNote, is a publicly traded software, data, and media company headquartered in Washington, D.C. The company was founded by Timothy Hwang, Gerald Yao, and Jonathan Chen in 2013. FiscalNote provides software tools, platforms, data services, and news through the FiscalNote Government Relationship Management (GRM) service, its core product. The company also uses an artificial intelligence platform to analyze proposed U.S. legislation based on key phrases, comparison to similar bills, lists of strengths and weaknesses, a timeline of the committees it has passed, information about the bill's sponsors, and

about: AI and data science services firm founded in Mumbai, now based in New York, offering analytics, AI products and consulting to large companies in finance, retail and healthcare. Customers are enterprises. B2B brand, with limited awareness. Customers are large corporations seeking analytics and decision systems. Employs several thousand staff. B2B brand with limited public awareness. Fractal has about 5,000 employees and offices in the US, India and Europe, and customers include large global companies.

wiki.title: Fractal
wiki.text: In mathematics, a fractal is a geometric shape containing detailed structure at arbitrarily small scales, usually having a fractal dimension strictly exceeding the topological dimension. Many fractals appear similar at various scales, as illustrated in successive magnifications of the Mandelbrot set. This exhibition of similar patterns at increasingly smaller scales is called self-similarity, also known as expanding symmetry or unfolding symmetry; if this replication is exactly the same at every scale, as in the Menger sponge, the shape is called affine self-similar. Fractal geometry relates to the mathematical branch of measure theory by the

about: Stamford, Connecticut-based research and advisory firm founded 1979, selling research, conferences and consulting to technology and business leaders, famous for the Magic Quadrant. Revenue is about $6 billion. Listed on the NYSE (IT). B2B brand with high awareness among executives. Revenue is roughly $6 billion from research subscriptions and events. Gartner has about 20,000 employees and its research is used by CIOs and CEOs worldwide.

wiki.title: Gartner
wiki.text: Gartner, Inc. is an American research and advisory firm focusing on business and technology topics. Gartner provides its products and services through research reports, conferences, and consulting. Its clients include large corporations, government agencies, technology companies, and investment firms.

about: New York-based global professional services firm, spun out of GE in 2005, delivering finance, procurement, supply chain and AI-led operations services to large enterprises. Revenue is about $5 billion with about 125,000 employees. Listed on the NYSE (G). B2B brand. Active in banking, insurance, consumer goods and life sciences. Genpact employs roughly 125,000 people across more than 30 countries, with large delivery centres in India.

wiki.title: Genpact
wiki.text: Genpact Ltd. is an American information technology services, consulting, and outsourcing company headquartered in New York City, New York. Founded in Gurgaon, India, and legally domiciled in Bermuda, Genpact employs more than 125,000 people and provides services to clients in over 30 countries worldwide. Genpact is listed on the NYSE and generated revenues of US$5.08 billion in 2025.

about: Palo Alto-based enterprise AI search and assistant startup, founded 2019, connecting company apps for search and agents. Customers are large enterprises, paying subscriptions. Valued at about $7 billion. B2B brand with growing awareness. Founded in Palo Alto in 2019 by ex-Google engineers. Customers use it to search across Slack, Google Drive and other work apps. Revenue is subscription-based and growing quickly.

wiki.title: Gleaning
wiki.text: Gleaning is the act of collecting leftover crops in the field after harvest. During harvest, there is food that is left or missed often because it does not meet store standards for uniformity. Sometimes, fields are left because they were not economically profitable to harvest.

about: Tampa-based security operations firm with the GreyMatter platform, founded 2007, offering threat detection and response to enterprises. Valued at about $3.4 billion. B2B brand with growing awareness. Customers are enterprise security teams and managed security providers. Employs several hundred staff. B2B with limited awareness outside cybersecurity. ReliaQuest employs about 1,000 people and works with large enterprises and managed security providers.

wiki.title: ReliaQuest
wiki.text: ReliaQuest is an American cybersecurity technology company headquartered in Tampa, Florida, with offices in Salt Lake City, Las Vegas, London, Dublin and Pune, India. The company provides threat detection, investigation and response through its GreyMatter security platform, which employs artificial intelligence to automate many of those cybersecurity tasks.

about: San Francisco-based blockchain developer platform, founded 2017, providing APIs and node infrastructure to Web3 applications. Valued about $10 billion at peak. B2B brand. Customers are blockchain developers and crypto companies, paying subscription and usage fees. Valued at billions at its peak. Little consumer awareness. Alchemy provides node and data tools to developers and has thousands of customers including large exchanges.

wiki.title: Alchemy
wiki.text: Alchemy is an ancient branch of natural philosophy, a philosophical and protoscientific tradition that was once practised in China, India, the Muslim world, and Europe. In its Western form, alchemy is first attested in pseudepigraphical texts written in Greco-Roman Egypt during the first few centuries AD. Greek-speaking alchemists often named their craft "the Art" (τέχνη) or "Knowledge" (ἐπιστήμη), and it was often characterised as mystic (μυστική), sacred (ἱɛρά), or divine (θɛíα).

wiki.title: Alchemy (company)
wiki.text: Alchemy was an American independent global film distributor based in Los Angeles, California. The company acquired and distributed feature films, television series and specialty programming.

about: Reston, Virginia-based energy management and analytics company, providing building energy optimisation for retailers and enterprises. B2B. Customers are retailers, banks and real estate owners using its energy platform. B2B with little public awareness. Based in Reston, Virginia, the business is built around cloud software and sensors that reduce energy bills for multi-site customers such as retail chains and banks. The company has operated for over two decades and has a long history of working with national retailers on energy savings.

wiki.title: GridPoint
wiki.text: GridPoint is an American clean technology company based in Reston, Virginia, that provides energy management and sustainability services to enterprises and government agencies, such as electric utilities.

about: Bellevue, Washington-based AI-powered contract management software company, founded 2009 in India, selling Icertis Contract Intelligence to large enterprises. Valued over $5 billion. B2B. Customers are large global enterprises, paying subscriptions. Has sponsored sports events in the US, but the brand is mainly B2B. Icertis serves large organisations in life sciences, banking and manufacturing, and has about 1,500 employees. Revenue comes from subscriptions to its contract intelligence cloud.

wiki.title: Icertis
wiki.text: Icertis is an American privately owned software company that provides contract management software to enterprise businesses using a software-as-a-service model. The company, which was founded in 2009, is headquartered in Bellevue, Washington.

about: San Francisco-based healthcare data and AI software company, founded 2014, serving health systems and payers. Valued around $3.5 billion. B2B. Customers are health systems and payers, paying for software and analytics. B2B with moderate awareness in US healthcare. Founded 2014 by Abhinav Shashank; operates in the US and India. Innovaccer employs a few thousand people and sells its platform to hospitals, health plans and government health programmes across the US.

wiki.title: Innovaccer
wiki.text: Innovaccer Inc. is an American healthcare technology company. Innovaccer was founded in 2014 and is headquartered in San Francisco, California. The company offers an agentic AI platform that unifies clinical, operational, and financial data across health systems, payers, government health agencies, and life sciences organizations. It provides autonomous AI agents and AI-powered software across population health management, revenue cycle management, payer risk and quality, utilization management, patient engagement, and public sector health programs. By 2026, Innovaccer described its overarching strategy as "The Agentic Cloud for Healthcare."

about: Perth-based Australian rare earths producer, owner of Mt Weld mine in Western Australia and the Kalgoorlie processing plant, and Malaysian processing. Largest rare earths producer outside China. Listed on the ASX (LYC). B2B. Customers are magnet and electronics makers, mostly outside China. Revenue about AUD 500-900 million. Strategic importance, low consumer awareness. Lynas has its processing plant in Malaysia and a heavy rare earths separation unit in Texas planned, and it supplies neodymium and praseodymium.

Chicago-based Azure management software firm, founded 2010, serving managed service providers with Nerdio Manager for MSP. B2B. Customers are managed service providers and enterprises. Revenue is subscription-based. B2B with limited awareness. Based in Chicago, Nerdio was founded by Vadim Vladimirskiy and Arjan Deepak. It sells software that helps MSPs deploy and cost-optimise Azure Virtual Desktop and Microsoft 365 for end customers, earning subscription fees. It raised a large growth round from Mainsail and others, and has a loyal partner base but almost no brand awareness outside IT channel circles.

wiki.title: Nerdio
wiki.text: Nerdio is an American Information Technology (IT) company headquartered in Chicago that specialises in providing virtual desktop implementations for businesses. The company provides streaming IT and IT-as-a-service to small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs).

about: Raleigh-based product analytics software firm, founded 2013, helping software teams understand and guide users, valued about $2.6 billion. B2B. Customers are software product teams at enterprises, paying subscriptions. Raised over $570 million. B2B with limited consumer awareness. Based in Raleigh, North Carolina, Pendo was founded in 2013. Customers use it to track in-app behaviour, onboard users and gather feedback. B2B brand with a loyal following among product managers; valued at about $2.6 billion.

wiki.title: Pendo
wiki.text: Pendo is a Kenyan drama television series that airs on NTV and premiered on 3 December 2014. The series is written by Grace Danile and produced and distributed by DIL Pictures.

about: San Francisco-based contact centre software company, founded 2011, selling the Talkdesk cloud platform and AI agents to enterprises for customer service in healthcare, retail and financial services. Customers pay subscriptions per seat across dozens of countries. Backed by Franklin Templeton and Whale Rock, valued at about $10 billion at its peak. B2B brand with limited public awareness. Its main products are Talkdesk CX Cloud and an AI-powered virtual agent product, and it has thousands of customers worldwide.

West Palm Beach, Florida cloud infrastructure provider, founded 2014, offering virtual machines, bare metal, GPU compute and AI cloud services to developers and enterprises from dozens of data centre locations. Revenue comes from usage-based billing. Privately held, valued at about $3.5 billion after 2025 funding. B2B brand with moderate awareness among developers. Vultr operates data centres in about 32 locations and has hundreds of thousands of customers worldwide, including AI start-ups using its GPUs.

wiki.title: Vultr
wiki.text: Vultr is an American cloud computing company that provides cloud infrastructure and is headquartered in West Palm Beach, Florida. The company provides cloud compute, cloud storage, cloud networking, GPU-as-a-service and bare metal-as-a-service. It operates data centers in over 30 regions worldwide.

about: London-based blockchain analytics company, founded 2013, providing crypto wallet screening and investigation tools to banks, exchanges and regulators for compliance and anti-money-laundering. Backed by SoftBank, Paladin and others, with around $220 million raised. B2B brand with moderate awareness in finance and crypto circles. The company serves customers in over 50 countries. Elliptic Lens and Navigator tools are used by exchanges, banks and law enforcement and the company is based in London.

wiki.title: Ellipse
wiki.text: In mathematics, an ellipse is a plane curve surrounding two focal points, such that for all points on the curve, the sum of both distances to the two focal points is a constant. It generalizes a circle, which is the special type of ellipse in which the two focal points are the same. The elongation of an ellipse is measured by its eccentricity, a number ranging from to.

wiki.title: Elliptic (company)
wiki.text: Elliptic is a British blockchain analytics firm headquartered in London, with offices in New York and Singapore. The company was co-founded by Adam Joyce, Tom Robinson and James Smith in 2013. It is the first company to develop cryptoasset anti-money laundering and sanctions compliance tools based on blockchain analytics. Its clients are primarily financial institutions and crypto businesses, although it also provides blockchain investigation tools and data to government agencies. Customers have included cryptocurrency exchanges, banks, and government agencies.

about: Cantina Labs is a San Francisco-based social AI company developing AI characters and companion experiences, with funding of $190 million shown. Products and audience are not confirmed beyond the input. (Limited public information - check before outreach.) Details of products and customer numbers are not confirmed beyond the input. The input does not describe individual characters, user counts or revenue, so any outreach should confirm the business first.

about: Singapore-based sustainability reporting software company, formerly a crypto financial services firm (Diginex), now selling ESG data and reporting platforms to corporates, listed on Nasdaq (DGNX). Total funding shown is about $197 million. B2B with low consumer awareness. The listing is on Nasdaq, with offices in Singapore and Hong Kong. Diginex has about 100 staff, and its platform helps companies track emissions and supply chain data to meet regulations.

Omaha, Nebraska-based cryptocurrency wallet company, founded 2015, selling the self-custody Exodus app on desktop and mobile to retail users, with support for many coins and swaps. Listed on NYSE American (EXOD). Revenue comes from swap fees. Consumer crypto brand with niche awareness. Revenue is swap fees and a share of trading from partners. Exodus has over a million users and supports hardware wallet integrations, with a team spread across several countries.

London-based fintech software company, founded in Romania in 2017, selling a low-code platform for banks, insurers and lenders to build digital onboarding and products. Customers are financial institutions. Raised about $179 million. B2B with low consumer awareness. Offices are in London and Romania, and its products are sold to retail banks and insurers. FintechOS's customers include banks and insurers in Europe, and it uses AI-assisted product design tools.

New York-based developer of the Uniswap protocol, the largest decentralised crypto exchange on Ethereum, founded 2018 by Hayden Adams. Builds the Uniswap app and wallet, earning fees from the interface. Raised about $178 million. Strong brand in crypto circles. Product use is high, with the Uniswap protocol routing tens of billions of dollars in monthly volume. Uniswap Labs employs a few hundred people and has launched its own wallet, API and the Unichain layer-2 network.

wiki.title: Uniswap
wiki.text: Uniswap is a decentralized cryptocurrency exchange protocol built on the Ethereum blockchain. It enables the automated trading of digital assets through smart contracts, eliminating the need for intermediaries or centralized order books. Uniswap facilitates cryptocurrency tokens swaps using liquidity pools contributed by users.

about: New York-based crypto quantitative risk management and yield optimisation firm, founded 2018, advising DeFi protocols such as Aave and Compound. Raised about $170 million. B2B with low consumer awareness. Customers are protocol treasuries and DAOs, who pay for risk and incentive management services. B2B only with no consumer awareness. Gauntlet's clients include major DeFi lenders and exchanges, and it advises them on parameters and incentives.

Einride is a Swedish freight technology company founded in 2016, known for its electric and autonomous trucks (the pod without a cab) and a freight-as-a-service platform with a logistics software layer. Customers include Maersk, Lidl, GE Appliances, Oatly and Bridgestone, and it operates in Sweden, the US and Europe. Based in Stockholm, it is backed by Nordic investors, EQT and Temasek-linked sources, and announced a SPAC merger with Legato Merger Corp. III in 2025 to list in the US. B2B but with visible branding on its futuristic trucks.

wiki.title: Einride
wiki.text: Einride AB is a Swedish transport company based in Stockholm, Sweden, specializing in electric and self-driving vehicles. The electric trucks are remotely controlled by drivers, and are notable for their lack of a driver's cab.

about: Alto Neuroscience is a US clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company using brain biomarkers and AI to match patients to treatments for psychiatric conditions such as depression, schizophrenia and bipolar disorder. Its drug candidates include ALTO-100, ALTO-300 and ALTO-203. Based in Mountain View, California, it listed on the NYSE (ANRO) in early 2024 after raising hundreds of millions in venture funding. Pre-revenue biotech with no consumer brand awareness.

BDx Data Centers is a Singapore-based operator of carrier-neutral data centres across Asia, with facilities in Indonesia, Hong Kong, Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand and Vietnam, serving cloud providers, telcos and enterprises. It was funded by private investors (funding shown at 475 million dollars). B2B infrastructure with no consumer brand profile; weak sponsorship fit.

about: Beacon Holdings is a holding company based in Toronto, Ontario, Canada. Crunchbase says it specialises in the AI sector and lists artificial intelligence as its industry. Funding shown is about 475 million dollars. The business, its subsidiaries and customers cannot be confirmed from the data given. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)
cb_desc: Beacon Holdings is a holding company that specializes in t...

about: Handshake is a San Francisco career network for students and recent graduates, connecting students at more than 1,500 US colleges with employers and recruiters, and expanding into AI data labelling through expert networks. Founded in 2014, it has about 18 million students and alumni users and raised funding of around 495 million dollars from Spark, Kleiner Perkins and others. Revenue comes from employers and from AI labs buying data work. Well known among US students and campus recruiters, little awareness outside.

wiki.title: Handshake
wiki.what: Short human greeting or parting ritual
wiki.text: A handshake is a globally widespread, brief greeting or parting tradition in which two people grasp one of each other's hands, and in most cases, it is accompanied by a brief up-and-down movement of the grasped hands. Customs surrounding handshakes are specific to cultures. Different cultures may be more or less likely to shake hands, or there may be different customs about how or when to shake hands.

wiki.title: Handshake (company)
wiki.text: Handshake is an American employment website for job listings, primarily for college students, launched in 2014. The platform is designed to help students find jobs or internships.

about: humans& is a frontier AI research company based in Redwood City, California, founded in 2025 by a team of researchers from major AI labs. It reportedly raised a very large seed round of about 480 million dollars in early 2026. The company focuses on building human-centred AI systems that collaborate with people. Early-stage and pre-revenue, B2B oriented, with limited public product information so far.
cb_desc: humans& operates as a frontier artificial intelligence research...

about: Kandou AI (Kandou Bus) is a Swiss semiconductor company based in Lausanne that designs high-speed, low-power chip-to-chip connectivity (retimers and links) for data centre, AI and automotive applications, originally spun from EPFL research on Chord signaling. Customers are chipmakers and system makers. Funding of about 505 million dollars is shown. B2B component designer with no consumer brand awareness.
cb_desc: Kandou Al specializes in the design of high-speed, and pin.

about: Locus Robotics is a US maker of autonomous mobile robots (LocusBots) that work alongside pickers in warehouses, sold as a robots-as-a-service model to retail, logistics and e-commerce operators including DHL, GEODIS and Boots. Founded in 2014 as a spin-off from Quiet Logistics, it is based in Wilmington, Massachusetts, and has raised over 460 million dollars, including a SoftBank-led round. B2B technology with low consumer awareness.

Multiverse is a London-based edtech company providing apprenticeships and workforce upskilling in AI, data and technology, with training delivered to employees at large companies such as Microsoft, Citi and Capital One. Founded in 2016 by Euan Blair, it has raised about 484 million dollars from SoftBank, StepStone and Lightspeed and reached a unicorn valuation of 1.7 billion dollars. Customers are enterprises and the learners they sponsor in the UK and US. Moderate profile among HR and corporate learning buyers.

wiki.title: Multiverse
wiki.text: The multiverse is the hypothetical set of all universes. Together, these universes are presumed to comprise everything that exists: the entirety of space, time, matter, energy, information, and the physical laws and constants that describe them. The different universes within the multiverse are referred to variously as: "parallel universes", "flat universes", "other universes", "alternate universes", "multiple universes", "plane universes", "parent and child universes", "many universes", or "many worlds". One common assumption is that the multiverse is a "patchwork quilt of separate universes all bound by the same laws of physics."

wiki.title: Multiverse (company)
wiki.text: Multiverse is a British educational technology company founded in 2016 by Euan Blair and Sophie Adelman. Based in London, United Kingdom, the company provides apprenticeship-based training and upskilling for early-career and experienced employees, primarily in technology and artificial intelligence roles. Multiverse works with employers to assess skills gaps within their workforce and delivers training programmes aligned with organisational needs.

about: Veritone is a Denver-based AI software company whose aiWARE platform runs machine-learning models for media, entertainment, public safety and government customers, providing tools for content search, licensing, advertising and legal evidence management. Listed on Nasdaq (VERI), it was founded in 2014 in Costa Mesa, California, and has raised about 530 million dollars. Revenue is around 100 million dollars. B2B with low consumer awareness, though clients include major broadcasters and sports organisations.

wiki.title: Veritone
wiki.text: Veritone, Inc. is an American artificial intelligence technology company based in Irvine, California founded in 2014. The company provides software services to the public and private sectors, including media, government, and law enforcement.

about: 2U is a US education technology company that works with universities to build and run online degree programs and boot camps, taking a share of tuition revenue. It owns the edX online learning marketplace, which it purchased in 2021 for 800 million dollars. Based in Arlington (Lanham), Maryland, it was listed on Nasdaq (TWOU) before filing for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in July 2024 and became privately held after restructuring. Customers are universities and students. Name familiarity is mostly within higher-education.

wiki.title: 2U (company)
wiki.text: 2U is an American educational technology company that contracts with non-profit colleges, universities, and companies to build, deliver, and support online degree and non-degree programs. 2U is the parent company of edX.

about: Arena is a San Francisco AI platform, previously LMArena, which lets users compare AI models head to head and ranks them via crowdsourced votes, used by labs such as OpenAI, Google and Anthropic. Founded as a UC Berkeley research project in 2023, it raised funding of about 450 million dollars in 2025 and 2026 at a multi-billion valuation. Customers are AI companies and enterprises. Well known inside the AI community, little general consumer awareness.

wiki.title: Arena
wiki.text: An arena is a large enclosed venue, often circular or oval-shaped, designed to showcase theatre, musical performances, or sporting events. It comprises a large open space surrounded on most or all sides by tiered seating for spectators, and may be covered by a roof. The key feature of an arena is that the event space is the lowest point, allowing maximum visibility. Arenas are usually designed to accommodate a multitude of spectators.
